sources.title: An overview of the Location Referencing toolbox
An overview of the Configuration toolset

tools.name: Append Events
tools.description: Appends event records from a table, layer, or feature class to an existing LRS event feature class.

tools.name: Append Routes
tools.description: Appends routes from an input polyline layer into an LRS Network.

tools.name: Apply Event Behaviors
tools.description: Updates the event locations for all event feature classes registered with the input network based on the route edit performed.

tools.name: Calculate Intersecting Route Measures
tools.description: Creates a table of all the routes and measures at each intersection location.

tools.name: Calculate Route Concurrencies
tools.description: Calculates and reports concurrent route sections in an LRS Network.

tools.name: Configure Address Feature Classes
tools.description: Configures the Address Range and Site Address Point feature classes from the Address Data Management solution for use with a linear referencing system (LRS) and the ArcGIS Roads and Highways extension.

tools.name: Configure External Event Behaviors With LRS
tools.description: Configures an external event in an LRS without connecting to an external event system.

tools.name: Configure External Event With LRS
tools.description: Associates event data stored in an external system with an LRS.

tools.name: Configure Lookup Table
tools.description: Configures a lookup table for one or more fields used in a multifield route ID.

tools.name: Configure Route Dominance Rules
tools.description: Configures a set of rules to determine the dominant route in a network where there are concurrent routes.

tools.name: Configure Utility Network Feature Class
tools.description: Configures the ArcGIS Utility Network Pipeline Line feature class for use with a linear referencing system (LRS).

tools.name: Configure Utility Network Feature Classes
tools.description: Configures the ArcGIS Utility Network Pipeline Line, Pipeline Device, and Pipeline Junction feature classes for use with a linear referencing system (LRS).

tools.name: Create LRS
tools.description: Creates an ArcGIS Location Referencing linear referencing system (LRS) and minimum schema items in a specified workspace.

tools.name: Create LRS Event
tools.description: Creates line or point events for an existing LRS Network.

tools.name: Create LRS Event From Existing Dataset
tools.description: Registers an existing feature class as an LRS event.

tools.name: Create LRS From Existing Dataset
tools.description: Creates a linear referencing system (LRS) in the specified workspace using existing datasets.

tools.name: Create LRS Intersection
tools.description: Creates an intersection feature class for an existing LRS Network.

tools.name: Create LRS Intersection From Existing Dataset
tools.description: Registers an existing intersection feature class as an intersection.

tools.name: Create LRS Network
tools.description: Creates an LRS Network in an ArcGIS Location Referencing linear referencing system (LRS).

tools.name: Create LRS Network From Existing Dataset
tools.description: Creates an LRS Network using an existing polyline feature class.

tools.name: Delete Routes
tools.description: Deletes routes and associated data elements from the LRS Network.

tools.name: Derive Event Measures
tools.description: Populates and updates the DerivedRouteID field and measure values on point and line events with those fields configured and enabled.

tools.name: Disable Derived Measure Fields
tools.description: Disables fields that store the derived network route ID, route name, and measure fields.

tools.name: Disable Referent Fields
tools.description: Disables referent fields for an existing linear referencing system (LRS) event feature class or feature layer. It does not delete the referent columns; it removes the referent column information from the Lrs_Metadata table.

tools.name: Disable Stationing Fields
tools.description: Disables stationing fields for the registered LRS event.

tools.name: Enable Derived Measure Fields
tools.description: Enables fields to store the derived route ID, derived route name, and derived measure fields for the specified LRS event feature class.

tools.name: Enable Referent Fields
tools.description: Enables or modifies the referent fields so that you can manage referent information for the registered LRS event.

tools.name: Enable Stationing Fields
tools.description: Enables or modifies stationing fields so that you can manage stationing information for the registered LRS event.

tools.name: Generate Calibration Points
tools.description: Generates calibration points for any route shape provided, including complex shapes such as self-closing, self-intersecting, and branched routes.

tools.name: Generate Events
tools.description: Regenerates shapes for event features registered with an LRS Network.

tools.name: Generate Intersections
tools.description: Generates new intersections and updates existing intersections.

tools.name: Generate Linear Referenced Feature Count
tools.description: Creates a feature count data product for routes in an LRS Network without an LRS data template.

tools.name: Generate Linear Referenced Length Summary
tools.description: Creates a length data product for routes in an LRS Network without an LRS data template.

tools.name: Generate Linear Referenced Route Log
tools.description: Creates a route log data product for routes in an LRS Network without an LRS data template.

tools.name: Generate LRS Data Product
tools.description: Transforms LRS data to create a length, route log, or feature count data product for routes in an LRS Network.

tools.name: Generate Routes
tools.description: Recreates shapes and applies calibration changes for route features in an LRS Network.

tools.name: Modify Event Behavior Rules
tools.description: Modifies event behavior rules for the registered event layer or feature class.

tools.name: Modify LRS
tools.description: Modifies an existing linear referencing system (LRS) in the specified workspace.

tools.name: Modify LRS Event
tools.description: Modifies properties of a linear referencing system (LRS) event.

tools.name: Modify LRS Intersection
tools.description: Modifies the properties of an intersection feature class, such as fields and intersecting layers, that compose the intersection feature class and can be added or removed.

tools.name: Modify LRS Network
tools.description: Modifies an LRS Network in a Location Referencing linear referencing system (LRS).

tools.name: Modify Network Calibration Rules
tools.description: Modifies the network calibration rules for an LRS Network.

tools.name: Modify Route ID Padding
tools.description: Modifies the padding, null, and length properties for fields that are part of a multifield route ID.

tools.name: Overlay Events
tools.description: Overlays one or more line and point event layers onto a target network and outputs a feature class or table that represents the dynamic segmentation of the inputs.

tools.name: Remove LRS Entity
tools.description: Removes a linear referencing system (LRS) entity from an input geodatabase workspace.

tools.name: Remove Overlapping Centerlines
tools.description: Removes overlapping centerline sections to ensure that there is one common centerline when centerline geometry overlaps.

tools.name: Reverse Line Orders
tools.description: Reverses the line order for all the routes in a line.

tools.name: Translate Event Measures
tools.description: Translates the measures (m-values) of a point or line event layer from one linear referencing method (LRM) to another.

tools.name: Update Measures From LRS
tools.description: Populates or updates the route and measure attributes on any point or line features, including Utility Network features such as pipes, devices, and junctions, or LRS features such as events and intersections.

terms.definition: Often used in the context of edit activities, which are discrete capabilities supported by ArcGIS Roads and Highways to edit LRS Networks. Roads and Highways supports the following edit activities: create route, extend route, realign route, cartographic realignment of route, reassign route, and retire route.
Experience Builder is a web app builder powered by ArcGIS Enterprise. It includes a suite of Location Referencing widgets that support the visualization, querying, and editing of LRS data.
In linear referencing, an asset refers to a type of linear-referenced event that represents a physical object, such as a milepost, pipe segment, or pipe fitting.
A route with a geometry that branches, so that you cannot traverse the entirety of the route without re-traversing at least one portion of the route.

A point feature that defines the measure for a specific location on an LRS route. Roads and Highways uses calibration points to define the measures on the routes. The measures between two calibration points on a route are derived by linear interpolation.

A polyline feature that defines part (or all) of the geometry of an LRS route. Routes in Roads and Highways can share centerlines in the same network (as is the case for concurrent, overlapping, or common routes) or routes in separate networks.
A route with a geometry that self-closes, self-intersects, or branches. Examples include loop routes, cul-de-sac type routes, branch routes, and cloverleaf ramp type routes.

A data scenario in which two or more routes in the same LRS Network share part or all of a centerline for their shape. Note that two routes with different centerlines are not considered a concurrency, even if they share the same geographic location.
Functionality in Roads and Highways that improves support for a multiuser enterprise geodatabase LRS Network and event editing by coordinating route and event edits.
A network composed of routes with continuous, uninterrupted measures that increase as you traverse the route. There are no equation points or stationing in a continuous network.

A network composed of multiple routes logically grouped in lines that can increase or decrease in measure as you traverse them. Equation points are used at locations where one route ends and another route begins. Events on engineering networks can span routes. In Roads and Highways, an engineering network is called an LRS Line Network.

During LRS edit activities, gaps or overlaps in measures can be introduced between the adjacent routes in a Line Network. These points of discontinuity in measures between the routes are referred to as equations.

In the context of linear referencing, an event refers to data that is located by its association to an LRS route and measure location. There are two event types. Point events have a single measure along a route, while linear events have a start and end measure along a route. Events are typically modeled in a database with a column for the route ID the record references, a measure column for the location on the route (two measure columns if it's a linear event), and a value (speed limit). Additional temporal information can also be modeled on the time frames to ensure that the event is valid.

In the context of linear referencing and Roads and Highways, event behavior refers to the configuration that defines how event measures and route associations respond to changes or edits in the LRS Network.

Event locks are a capability in Roads and Highways conflict prevention that allow a user to prevent other users from editing events for an event layer on a specific route. When events for an event layer on a route are locked, only the lock owner can edit those events on the route in the version the lock was acquired. Other users can acquire event locks for the same route on a different event layer, if needed. To release an event lock, you must post changes to the locked events to the lock root version. If any event locks exist for a route, no one can edit the route until all event locks are released.

Linear or point events that reside inside the geodatabase where the LRS is configured. When registered, Roads and Highways creates an event feature class and manages the shape of the feature based on the route, measure, and start and end dates.
A continuous logical grouping of one or more routes used for a measure system, specifically used in conjunction with an LRS Line Network.
An event that represents a segment of a route from a starting measure (or From Measure) to an ending measure (or To Measure).

Acronym for linear referencing method, a method for defining measurements along linear features for the purpose of linear referencing. Examples of LRMs are State Mile Point, County Mile Point, or Project Stationing.

Acronym for linear referencing system, the method of storing geographic locations by using relative positions along a measured linear feature. The linear referencing system implemented by Roads and Highways on ArcGIS technology supports multiple linear referencing methods and event measure behaviors.

A .csv file or geodatabase table that is generated by transforming LRS data. The .csv file or geodatabase table can be used in a reporting solution of your choice, such as the reporting tools in ArcGIS Pro and others.
A network generated from a Line Network. In a Derived Network, routes that belong to the same line are merged together to create one route with a beginning measure of zero.
A logical grouping of routes to a line where the measure can increase or decrease monotonically. This type of network supports events that span routes and also supports equations.
A collection of routes, measured to a specific LRM in Roads and Highways.
A location along a route based on a distance from a known point of origin.
An event that represents a single point location on a route at a specific measure.
A system of stationing in which the starting reference station is established at the base of a project location, and all distances along the route centerline are measured from that point location.
A feature in Roads and Highways that can be added to the redline feature class and can be used to communicate desired modifications to the LRS Network.
A fixed location along a route that has a discrete measure value from which other locations are determined.
A fixed distance from a referent. The referent offset can be positive or negative.
An event whose location is modeled as being a specific distance along a route relative to another event on the route.

A linear LRS feature. In Roads and Highways, a route is a roadway where measure values are strictly increasing or decreasing monotonically. Routes are polyline features that contain m-measures and are built on centerlines that are polyline features that do not contain m-measures.
Rules configured for each LRS Network used to determine which route is the primary, or dominant, route when there is a concurrency. Configuration of these rules is optional.

Route locks are a capability in Roads and Highways conflict prevention that allows a user to prevent other users from editing a route and events on a route while the route is being edited. When a route is locked, only the lock owner can edit the route and events on the route in the version the lock was acquired. To release a lock on a route, you must post changes to the route and events on the route to the lock root version.

Reference points with numerical values that are placed along the horizontal measurement of a route, centerline, or baseline at a regular interval. Station numbers increase from west to east or south to north based on the cardinal direction of the overall network.

The fundamental system of measurement used by surveyors. For highway or pipeline projects, a starting reference station is first established; then all distances along the route centerline are measured from that point location. Generally, the distance between two adjoining stations along a route is 100 feet. The first station located at the beginning of the baseline is 0+00 and the next station located 100 feet away from it is 1+00. For example, a station number of 10+34.05 depicts 1034.05 feet (10*100 + 34.05) away from the starting station.
